entries.summary: Introduced governance/change_log.json as a passive, non-enforcing per-repo change tracker (federation-wide rollout across all seven repos). It documents changes only; nothing reads or validates it, and nothing in CI depends on its contents. Prompted by removing a repo-wide change-freeze that existed in moneysweep-pr and ovnis-pr's unified-skillpack conformance checks and blocked ordinary PRs; this repo never had that freeze.

Adopted the change-coupled documentation gate defined by thehub-pr ADR 0010: the shared tools/check_docs_sync.py, a docs-sync workflow, a Claude Code Stop hook, CLAUDE.md, a "Documentation stays true" section in CONTRIBUTING.md, and this repo's .federation/docs-sync.json. Re-pinned PRII_TEMPLATE_REF to thehub-pr 09e2e54, which carries the checker's fix for path:symbol references. The pre-commit hook and PR-template line this repo does not render from the hub were added by hand. Tooling and workflow change only: no contract, schema or dependency edge changed. PROVISIONAL until docs-sync is a required status check on main.

Re-pinned PRII_TEMPLATE_REF to thehub-pr 4258c3c, which hardens the shared docs-sync checker (thehub-pr#359): a pull request can no longer exempt itself through exempt_authors, manifest hygiene is judged on the head manifest so retiring a coupling or renaming a coupled doc no longer fails, a glob that matches nothing now fails when the change adds it, and a :symbol or :line locator is dropped from Markdown link targets. CONTRIBUTING.md now states what the gate enforces. The manifest comment now says a coupling fires on its on events. Tooling and documentation change only: no contract, schema or dependency edge changed.

Added the Inland and Off-Shore Access Point registries (spiderweb/access_points), their read-only /v1/access-points API and map workspace, three JSON schemas, the committed registry documents and their deterministic builder. Hardened three pre-existing gates so that a placeholder vertical datum no longer counts as a stated datum, a rootless direct observation no longer outranks a rooted one, and an undeclared datum no longer passes datum policy. No record is exported to the hub, no tile source is registered, no write endpoint exists and federation.json is unchanged. The acronyms ILAP and OSAP keep their existing meanings; the new registries use the namespaces access_point.inland and access_point.offshore (docs/ACCESS_POINT_TERMINOLOGY_DECISION.md). Release state is recorded in evidence/access_points/certification_report_v1.json: software tested, science exploratory, production not authorised.

Added planned, bounded, metadata-only source-discovery runs for the access-point registries (spiderweb/access_points/discovery.py, scripts/discover_access_point_sources.py) and the search boxes they use (configs/access_point_discovery_corridors.yaml). A search box is never a feature position: the corridor file is refused if it states a coordinate, a depth or a feature, and the five off-shore seeds stay without geometry. The registry builder now reads the sealed source catalogue of the current run, when one is committed, and registers its surveys as references only. A live transport with a generic user agent, a response-header allow-list and redirect refusal was added. One run was executed on 2026-11-16 under an explicit grant from the repository owner (48 metadata requests to three public NOAA catalogue hosts, 180 surveys listed, exact response bytes kept under evidence/access_points/source_discovery/2026-11-16); the registries now hold those surveys as references and no feature, status or coordinate changed. The elevation-inventory adapter now cites only a real address where the inventory publishes an HTML fragment. No data product is downloaded by any code path, nothing is exported to the hub and federation.json is unchanged. Release state is recorded in evidence/access_points/certification_report_v2.json.
